scenes.text: Most questions an AI app gets are easy, but every one of them goes to a big, expensive model. You pay big-model prices for small-model work.
Meet Apprentice: an open-source gateway where small open models learn from big ones, so your app gets cheaper every day.
Your app sends a normal OpenAI request. Apprentice gives it first to the student: Qwen three, a small open model running right on a laptop.
A judge checks every answer. It's Kev, a small open model we fine-tuned to spot wrong answers, raising its accuracy from forty-six to ninety-nine percent.
If the judge isn't confident, the request goes up to the teacher, the large open model G L M five point two.
Every teacher answer is saved to memory. When a similar question comes back, the student sees that example, and gets it right on its own.

On eighty held-out questions, the student alone scored twenty-five percent. After learning, Apprentice reached ninety-seven and a half percent accuracy, with eighty-six percent of requests on the small model, at eighty-seven percent lower cost than the teacher.
On question types it has never seen, it scores fifty-three percent, versus thirty-three for the student alone. So the judge still matters.
It fits anywhere questions repeat: store analytics, customer support, Hinglish kirana orders, coding agents, and private data that should stay on your own machine.
Every model is open weight: Qwen three, G L M five point two, Kev, and Nomic embeddings.
Point your OpenAI client at Apprentice with one line, and watch the student take over.
Apprentice. Small models that learn from big ones. Built at Hacktoberfest, Mumbai.
